target_customer: Urban households buying recurring and one-off home cleaning, later other home services
problem: Booking a trustworthy, vetted home cleaner was slow and unreliable. Homejoy let customers book online and matched them with interviewed, background-checked cleaners.
business_model: marketplace take rate on booked cleanings

founders.name: Adora Cheung
founders.background_notes: Per Wikipedia, the pair first explored Pathjoy, a life coach and therapist platform, before moving to cleaning.

founders.name: Aaron Cheung
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as a former founder and later CEO of Homeaglow. Prior employers and education not found.

exit.reason: Company cited profitability difficulty and four worker classification lawsuits. About 20 staff were hired by Google; this was not a company acquisition.

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking and scheduling marketplace with cleaner vetting. The hard parts were operational (supply quality, scheduling), not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Supply could be poached and customers moved directly to cleaners after first booking. Entrants such as Handy competed on the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acted. Handy was reported to have explored buying Homejoy in 2015 but talks broke down, and Google hired part of the team in July 2015.

market_need_then: Home cleaning was a large fragmented offline market with unreliable local providers. Wikipedia and the YC page show strong early demand, with 31 cities by 2013, though retention was poor.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Pathjoy to Homejoy in March 2013 to match the home cleaning mission. No source gives deeper origin.
branding.domain_note: homejoy.com now redirects to Homeaglow, the later company of Aaron Cheung.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and consumer friendly: everyone deserves a happy home.

rebrands.why: Fit the new home cleaning focus after the pivot, per TechCrunch coverage

branding.community_and_virality: Search showed no merch or fan community. Press covered the name change and the shutdown.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in tech press and in 30+ cities, but no distinct brand asset was found. Similar names like Housejoy in India appear in results, a mild confusion risk.

pivots.from: Pathjoy, matching customers with life coaches and therapists
pivots.why: Per Wikipedia the original idea was abandoned for cleaning

outcome_analysis: Homejoy grew fast after a 2013 raise of about 38 million dollars and reached 31 cities, but customer retention was poor and acquisition costs high, as the founder's own account and press describe. Four worker classification lawsuits scared off investors, and the company shut down in July 2015 after declining small offers. Critics also cite costly international expansion and cleaners moving off platform. Google hired about 20 staff.
notes: Directory status says Acquired but sources show a shutdown with an acquihire by Google of about 20 staff. The 38M round in Dec 2013 was reported as a combined Series A (Google Ventures lead) and Series B (Redpoint lead); sources disagree on leads, so it is recorded as stage other. Total raised reported around 40M. Competitors dated near the 2010 batch were not found; Handy, TaskRabbit and others appear in 2014 sources only (Handy and TaskRabbit as rivals from 2014 expansion coverage), so the list is empty. Founded year disagrees across sources (2010 vs 2012); YC batch is Summer 2010.
